planner_json.title: Install, load and invoke Grok on both tracks, with --trust only where no key exists
depends_on: GAW-1 (the adapter contract, declarations, stance table, probe runner and real-cli test harness this adapter builds on)
GAW-2 (the stop_at option its must-ask entry passes to the runtime)

write_prohibited: plugins/pixel-perfect/** - no plugin change in this task
Any keyed step in `.github/workflows/harness-eval.yml` except Grok's, which gains one line
Any file not listed in WRITE-ALLOWED

seed/pinned-grok.description: Grok at the pinned version installed by its own installer into a temp HOME with an allowlisted env and no Claude install beside it

specification.objective: Grok installs, loads and runs through the adapter contract on both tracks, with `--trust` only where no key exists.
specification.success_state: A keyless load at 1.0.46 in a temp HOME proves the installed plugin's digest equals the checkout's and lists 11 of 11 commands. Exactly one plan step holds `--trust`, and a keyed entry carrying it throws at build time. The registry serves this adapter, and the keyed step runs the denied-write probe on pinned.

requirements.description: GIVEN the pinned Grok CLI in a temp HOME with an allowlisted env and no Claude install beside it WHEN the adapter's keyless load runs against this checkout THEN `observed_cli_version` reads `1.0.46` with `identity_decision.ok` true, 11 of 11 command names are present, and `loaded_plugin_root` sits under the temp HOME's `.grok/installed-plugins`
requirements.verification_service: real Grok CLI at the pinned version in a temp HOME
requirements.positive_example: Fresh temp HOME: identity approved at 1.0.46, installed digest equal to the checkout digest, and all 11 command names among the 13 inspect returns.
requirements.red: On base the registry answers grok-adapter-not-implemented, no load runs, and the identity assertion fails.

scenario.verification_service: real Grok CLI at the pinned version in a temp HOME

would_fail_if: the test reads the real HOME, so a Claude-compatible plugin shadows the install
the digest is computed from the checkout twice
the list is a static array of names

build_proof.range: anything that proves the plugin Grok loads is byte-for-byte this checkout's on a machine with no Claude install
examples: hashing the installed-plugins directory the install created

steps: run the adapter's keyless load against this checkout in the temp HOME

requirements.description: GIVEN the adapter's plan and invocation table, and the real workflow file WHEN every plan step's argv and env are read, each graded and probe entry runs with every credential removed, and a keyed copy of an entry gains `--trust` before the table builds THEN exactly 1 step holds `--trust`, named `plugin-install`, with 0 credential names in its env, the keyed copy throws `trust-on-keyed-step`, and the required probe's prompt names `work/keep.txt`
requirements.verification_service: the real workflow file and the real guard and capture over the adapter's table
requirements.positive_example: plugin-install carries --trust and no key; each graded and probe entry's refusal capture holds no --trust, --always-approve or bypassPermissions.
requirements.red: On base no grok table exists, so reading argv from its persisted refusal captures fails.
